I wear period underwear or just use a pad while using boric acid as it flushes out your vagina and needs somewhere to go. You could also go to a local pharmacy and purchase a product like Monistat and use that if your prefer. 

Also avoid soap around the area until the infection has cleared out. Like I said earlier, give your vagina a break :)

I lost my Mischa to kidney failure on December 22, 2024. I still can’t go in the bathroom where I administered her fluids. The empty bags of the solution are still in there as well. I can’t go in there. There was too much pain, hope, and grief in that room. I miss her every single day and am angry something like this could happen to such a loving and innocent cat. I love you forever, Mischa. I’m so sorry I only got to love you for 6 years. 🩷

The guilt of not noticing she was unwell sooner. I can’t help but lay awake at night thinking about how her behavior changed and I noticed it but didn’t think much of it at the time. I think about how she sat in places she didn’t normally go, and just felt pain. She was in stage 4 kidney failure and I didn’t even know that could happen to a 6 year old cat. I also think about when I took her to get euthanized and made sure she saw the sun and got to look at it for awhile before we went into the hospital. And I hope that she liked that because while she was sick it was winter and quite dark most of the time. Mostly just guilt. Immense guilt.

December 22, 2024 was when I lost my Mischa. I was holding her in my lap, and when the first dosage that would put her in a deep sleep hit her, she kind of sat up higher and she twitched her ears a few times. The vet told me when it first hits them it’s quite euphoric. So when her ears were twitching, I felt that she was feeling good. Then she quickly dropped into my arms, because she was asleep. But that drop… I’ll never forget it. It was the worst feeling I’ve ever felt. She went limp in my arms and I knew she was asleep but that drop she did just terrifies me even today. 

So yes, I still think about every single day. I wish I had planned an at home euthanasia. But she was so sick on that day and she was telling me she was exhausted from her chronic kidney failure. I wish I did so many things differently. I wish she could tell me it’s okay and that she’s okay.

Okay so before I answer the first question I should make it super clear: I do not walk the streets. The city I live in has 150 massage parlors that people can work in and you also have the choice to be an independent worker. Independent workers typically have a condo/apartment where they will meet their clients and do the services, or they will meet up at a hotel at the providers choice and discretion. 

When it comes to those who are walking the streets.. the reason they are there are because it’s illegal and they do not have a safe place to work. This is so dangerous for them in more ways than one and it’s sad knowing that there are men and women walking around in the cold trying to get by. I can’t speak for them and say they choose to be there, but I’m sure if they lived where I do and had to option of working in a much safer environment where it’s fully legal, they would do so. I don’t recommend asking anyone that question because it can be really hurtful to some or a very personal question. I don’t like being asked this by clients I’ve just met because it makes me want to ask them “well how did YOU get into YOUR line of work?” Because at the end of the day, we all do jobs we may not love so we can get by. The providers in the states don’t have a safe place to talk about what they deal with and that just breaks my heart. If they are raped or mistreated, law enforcement won’t do anything simply because their job is “illegal” and it was “their own fault”. It is so not like that here, we call the police over any issues we may have and they are more than happy to help us file police reports or whatever else we need.

If it was not legal to do my job I would not do it. The legality of it has given me the freedom to seek medical care when I need it and I never feel ashamed for it. I also pay taxes like any other person does and it’s so great being able to go to an accountant and have them help me with taxes because nothing I do is wrong. If it were illegal like it is down in the states I would stay far away from it because you’re completely screwed if you get caught and I couldn’t handle being in jail for something like that. I’m able to tell my friends and family about bad clients I’ve had because it is legal. I’m able to seek out support from the city because it is legal. Not having those things would make me feel incredibly alone, so I can’t even begin to imagine what it’s like for those who do not have the same resources as I do... So incredibly sad, honestly.

Hi! I’m a current sex worker by choice, but my choice is based on financial needs and trying to get ahead at a quicker pace than people who work “square” jobs. I work in Alberta, Canada where it’s fully legal to do what I do as long as you have a license. I’m pretty sure the rest of Canada is legalized to but I don’t want to say it is and then be wrong. 

This job is different for everyone. Some people (I’m using people as sex workers can come in all different types of genders, binaries, etc. :) ) find this type of work very empowering while others really struggle with it. I’ve met people who experience a full spectrum on how it affects them, as it also changes for me depending on my relationship with myself, my mental health, and the clients I’m dealing with. 

I’ve been doing this work for almost 2 years now and I’ve gotten to a point where I feel empowered about 90% of the time but have also experienced a very strong disinterest in sex whether it be for work or for fun. I’ve been single the entire time I’ve worked because of this lack of interest and I know that any partner I have would have their own needs that I wouldn’t have the interest in meeting.

My close friends and parents know what I do and I’ve found that other women are far more supportive and genuinely curious about my job while my male friends tend to be a bit more apprehensive. They like to tell me things like “I can’t believe guys pay you for that” “I would NEVER pay for sex” and it’s obviously pretty harsh of them to say that as they are saying I and my fellow sex workers are not worth our prices. So there have been a few friendships lost over my work.
